ground_truth.node_text: Start

turns.utterance: Begin with a warm-up run. Bring the spindle up to fifty percent speed and let it run for ten minutes.

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Warm-up complete. Spindle ran at fifty percent for ten minutes.

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Mount a calibrated accelerometer on the front bearing housing using a flat washer stud or magnetic base. Run the spindle at three thousand RPM with no toolholder fitted and record the RMS vibration velocity in millimeters per second. Then repeat the measurement at maximum rated speed and compare both readings against the ISO 10816 zone limits for this machine class.

ground_truth.node_text: Mount a calibrated accelerometer on the front bearing housing with a flat washer stud or magnetic base. Run the spindle at 3000 revolutions per minute with no toolholder fitted and record the root mean square vibration velocity in millimetres per second. Repeat at the maximum rated speed and compare both readings against the ISO 10816 zone limits for this machine class.

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Accelerometer mounted and measurements taken at both speeds. I've recorded the vibration velocities and compared them to the ISO limits.

ground_truth.node_text: Mount a calibrated accelerometer on the front bearing housing with a flat washer stud or magnetic base. Run the spindle at 3000 revolutions per minute with no toolholder fitted and record the root mean square vibration velocity in millimetres per second. Repeat at the maximum rated speed and compare both readings against the ISO 10816 zone limits for this machine class.

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Is the vibration level below the alarm limit?

ground_truth.node_text: Vibration level below alarm limit?

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: The vibration is within limits, but I'm hearing a rhythmic knocking sound coming from the bearing housing that wasn't there before.

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Yes, both readings are comfortably below the alarm threshold.

ground_truth.node_text: Vibration level below alarm limit?

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Is the bearing temperature within the rated operating limit?

ground_truth.node_text: Bearing temperature within rated operating limit?

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Yes, the bearing temperatures on both front and rear housings are well within the acceptable range.

ground_truth.node_text: Bearing temperature within rated operating limit?

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Is the radial runout within two micrometer tolerance?

ground_truth.node_text: Radial runout within 2 µm tolerance?

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Yes, the total indicator reading shows runout is within the two micrometer spec.

ground_truth.node_text: Radial runout within 2 µm tolerance?

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Is the axial play within three micrometer tolerance?

ground_truth.node_text: Axial play within 3 µm tolerance?

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Actually, I'm seeing significant radial runout on the shaft here—the dial indicator is showing almost 15 microns of radial wobble, not axial movement.

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: No, the averaged axial deflection is reading about four point two micrometers, which exceeds the three micrometer limit.

ground_truth.node_text: Axial play within 3 µm tolerance?

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Adjust the preload spacer or shim to reduce the axial play.

ground_truth.node_text: Adjust pre load spacer or shim to reduce axial play

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Preload spacer adjusted. The axial play should be reduced now.

ground_truth.node_text: Adjust pre load spacer or shim to reduce axial play

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Apply a thin, even coat of engineer's blue to a clean test arbor with the correct taper angle. Insert the arbor, rotate it by hand under moderate axial load, then withdraw and inspect the contact pattern. The blue should transfer uniformly over at least seventy percent of the taper length.

ground_truth.node_text: Apply a thin even coat of engineer's blue to a clean test arbor with the correct taper angle for this spindle. Insert the arbor, rotate by hand under moderate axial load, then withdraw and inspect the contact pattern. The blue should transfer uniformly over at least 70% of the taper length; a spotted or narrow band pattern indicates taper bore damage or swarf contamination.

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Test arbor inserted and rotated. The blue transfer pattern looks good and uniform across the taper.

ground_truth.node_text: Apply a thin even coat of engineer's blue to a clean test arbor with the correct taper angle for this spindle. Insert the arbor, rotate by hand under moderate axial load, then withdraw and inspect the contact pattern. The blue should transfer uniformly over at least 70% of the taper length; a spotted or narrow band pattern indicates taper bore damage or swarf contamination.

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Is the taper contact pattern above eighty-five percent bearing area?

ground_truth.node_text: Taper contact pattern above 85% bearing area?

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Yes, I'm seeing contact coverage at approximately ninety percent of the taper surface.

ground_truth.node_text: Taper contact pattern above 85% bearing area?

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Is the drawbar retention force within the rated range?

ground_truth.node_text: Drawbar retention force within rated range?

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Yes, the dynamometer reading shows the drawbar force is right in the middle of the specified range.

ground_truth.node_text: Drawbar retention force within rated range?

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Is the thermal growth within the compensation model tolerance?

ground_truth.node_text: Thermal growth within compensation model tolerance?

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: No, the measured thermal displacement at stabilization is outside the expected range from the compensation table.

ground_truth.node_text: Thermal growth within compensation model tolerance?

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Complete the following checks: First, read the thermal compensation growth coefficient from the controller. Second, compare the stored values against the reference values for this spindle. Third, check whether the compensation parameters were modified since the last service.

ground_truth.node_text: Complete the following checks: 1. Read the thermal compensation growth coefficient from the controller. 2. Compare the stored values against the reference values for this spindle. 3. Check whether the compensation parameters were modified since last service.

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: I've pulled the compensation coefficients and compared them to the reference data. Found a discrepancy in the stored parameters.

ground_truth.node_text: Complete the following checks: 1. Read the thermal compensation growth coefficient from the controller. 2. Compare the stored values against the reference values for this spindle. 3. Check whether the compensation parameters were modified since last service.

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Reverify the thermal compensation after the parameter update.

ground_truth.node_text: Reverify thermal compensation after parameter update

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Hey, quick question – do we need to fill out a separate work order for the parts we replaced on the conveyor system yesterday, or does that go under the same maintenance ticket?

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Parameters updated and reverified. The thermal growth now matches the compensation model within tolerance.

ground_truth.node_text: Reverify thermal compensation after parameter update

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Is the spindle speed within plus or minus zero point one percent at all test speeds?

ground_truth.node_text: Spindle speed within ±0.1% at all test speeds?

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Yes, the tachometer readings at all three test speeds show errors well under zero point one percent.

ground_truth.node_text: Spindle speed within ±0.1% at all test speeds?

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Is the final vibration within the warning limit at full speed?

ground_truth.node_text: Final vibration within warning limit at full speed?

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: No, the vibration velocity at maximum speed shows an increase of about thirty-five percent compared to the baseline from the last service.

ground_truth.node_text: Final vibration within warning limit at full speed?

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Log all measurements and update the spindle maintenance record.

ground_truth.node_text: Log all measurements and update spindle maintenance record

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: All measurements logged and the maintenance record has been updated.

ground_truth.node_text: Log all measurements and update spindle maintenance record

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Procedure complete. Note that the elevated vibration at full speed requires bearing assessment before releasing the spindle to production. Document this finding in the work order.

ground_truth.node_text: End, Procedure complete

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Understood, I'll flag the spindle for bearing assessment before production release.

ground_truth.node_text: End, Procedure complete
